newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Awaiting PPI, lackluster FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Awaiting PPI, lackluster FOMC.

text.p: U.S. credit markets will likely keep their current burst of optimism on Wednesday as fresh data are expected to be friendly and the Federal Reserve is seen keeping short-term interest rates unchanged.

The market will have a full agenda, whose highlights include the release of the October Producer Price Index (PPI) at 0830 EST/1330 GMT and the gathering of the central bank's policy setting-arm, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
"We're expecting a friendly PPI report and we're not expecting the Fed to do anything," said Carol Stone, senior economist at Nomura Securties International Inc.
Analysts said the overall PPI number may bounce mildly as a recent run-up in energy prices is likely to put upward pressure on U.S. wholesale inflation.
Pundits said, however, the impact of higher prices for a variety of oil-related items could be somewhat offset by a drop in food prices, especially grains.
The core index, which excludes food and energy prices, is expected to remain mostly tame.
"The upcoming data on the price side should be pretty benign," said Wayne Ayers, chief economist at Bank of Boston.
In a Reuters survey, U.S. economists expect, on average, overall PPI to rise 0.2 percent in October. The core rate, which excludes food and energy price fluctuations, is seen up a tame 0.1 percent.

Players are also gearing up for the FOMC meeting. But the relatively stable economic outlook - featuring slower growth and low inflation - has taken away much of the luster of the Wednesday's gathering.
Some traders even expressed nostalgia for the last FOMC meeting on September 24 when analysts were mostly split about what the Fed would do and the outcome of the gathering was anybody's guess.
At that meeting, the Fed kept monetary policy on hold and maintained a 5-1/4 percent target for the federal funds rate.

"The market is too calm for a pre-FOMC meeting day," said a trader at a U.S. investment bank. "A more stable economic outlook has taken away much of the interest in tomorrow's (Wednesday's) meeting," he added.

The market will also take in the Atlanta Fed industry business activity index for October at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, which is expected to show the manufacturing sector is still growing at a moderate pace, analysts said.
"I guess there will be continuing signs of moderation in the manufacturing sector if there's something you want to read from the Atlanta report," Nomura's Stone said.

Market participants will also face some fresh supply with the auction of some $13.0 billion in 34-day Treasury bills. The government will also announce the terms and the amount of its monthly two- and five-year note auctions on Wednesday.
In late trading on Tuesday, the 6-1/2-percent benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was around the day's highs, quoted up 27/32 at 100-24/32. Its yield was at a fresh eight-month low at 6.44 percent.

The Federal Reserve added temporary reserves to the banking system on Tuesday via $2.0 billion customer repurchase agreements when the federal funds were at 5-3/8 percent, well above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target.
Fed funds are seen opening at 5.25 percent on Wednesday.
